scope: Public consumer image pricing and the proposed Midjourney-shaped four-tier template, compared with GALX's implemented creation, account, Stripe and fair-use contracts.

research.finding: Midjourney's familiar ladder is Basic, Standard, Pro and Mega, differentiated by a metered fast allowance, slower/unlimited modes and privacy/concurrency features.
Adobe makes a monthly generative-credit balance and reset explicit, which is a clearer pattern than hiding generation volume behind an ambiguous job count.

implemented_capabilities: One-time five-image welcome allowance for verified accounts
One active $10/month GALX Pro consumer subscription
One to four image outputs per request
Five supported aspect ratios and Standard/HD detail options
Owned library, Favorites, prompt reuse, downloads and public community discovery
Public-by-default creations with account sharing controls
not_currently_offered: Video generation or SD/HD video tiers
Fast, Relax or other customer-selectable queue modes
Stealth/private generation as a plan entitlement
Public Stripe prices or checkout contracts for four consumer tiers
decision: Use a truthful two-step ladder now: Start free with five outputs once, then GALX Pro at $10/month for ongoing image creation under fair-use terms. Keep the four-tier Basic/Standard/Pro/Mega shape as a future expansion hypothesis only; do not publish its unsupported video, privacy, queue, editor or concurrency promises.
ux_strategy: Make the free-to-paid decision the first comparison, with one primary action per option.
Use image outputs as the plain-language unit and state that a four-image batch uses four outputs.
Show supported controls once, in one comparison, instead of inventing separate feature gates.
Keep the current checkout and billing authority as the source of truth; a card is not an entitlement until its backend price, webhook reconciliation and usage policy exist.

checks.stripe_contract: existing Pro price and checkout preserved
checks.public_boundary: unsupported capabilities omitted from the active offer; retired private-integration guidance is not indexed as a public guide
checks.limitations: No Stripe products/prices or production deployment changed in this pass
